Titles, Labels & Text Styling

ggtitle(), labs(), captions, tags, axis text, and full element_text() control

Master ggplot2 plot labelling — titles, subtitles, captions, tags, axis labels, and how to style every text element with element_text().

Overview

Two main ways to add labels in ggplot2:

  • ggtitle() — dedicated title + subtitle function
  • labs() — set title, subtitle, caption, tag, axis labels, and legend titles all at once

Title

Using ggtitle()

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  ggtitle("US Unemployment Over Time")

Using labs()

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "US Unemployment Over Time")

Title position

Default: aligned to the panel (plot data area).
Set "plot" to align to the full figure including margins.

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Aligned to full plot width") +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")   # "panel" | "plot"

Subtitle

# Option 1 — ggtitle()
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  ggtitle("Title of the plot",
          subtitle = "Subtitle of the plot")

# Option 2 — labs()
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title    = "Title of the plot",
       subtitle = "Subtitle of the plot")

Caption

Captions appear at the bottom-right by default. Great for data source attribution.

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title   = "US Unemployment",
       caption = "Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics")

# Move caption to left
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(caption = "Source: BLS") +
  theme(plot.caption.position = "plot",
        plot.caption           = element_text(hjust = 0))  # 0=left, 1=right

Tag

Tags are placed at the top-left. Useful for labelling panels (A, B, C…) in multi-panel figures.

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "US Unemployment", tag = "Fig. 1")

# Change tag position
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(tag = "A") +
  theme(plot.tag.position = "bottomright")
  # options: "topleft","top","topright","left","right","bottomleft","bottom","bottomright"

All labels in one labs() call

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Width, y = Petal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species) +
  labs(
    title    = "Petal Width by Species",
    subtitle = "Iris dataset · faceted by species",
    caption  = "Source: R built-in iris dataset",
    tag      = "Fig. 1",
    x        = "Sepal Width (cm)",
    y        = "Petal Width (cm)",
    fill     = "Iris Species"
  )

Axis Labels

# Simple axis labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  xlab("Weight (1,000 lbs)") +
  ylab("Miles per Gallon")

# Remove axis labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)

# Rotate x-axis tick labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = row.names(mtcars), y = mpg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))

# Remove axis tick text
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

Styling Text with element_text()

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title    = "Vehicle Weight vs Fuel Economy",
    subtitle = "Each dot is one car model from the 1974 Motor Trend magazine",
    caption  = "Source: Motor Trend US, 1974",
    x        = "Weight (1,000 lbs)",
    y        = "Miles per Gallon"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(
      family     = "serif",       # Font family
      face       = "bold",        # "plain","bold","italic","bold.italic"
      colour     = "#0e0f14",
      size       = 18,
      hjust      = 0,             # 0=left, 0.5=centre, 1=right
      vjust      = 1,
      lineheight = 1.2,
      margin     = margin(b = 8)  # space below title
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, colour = "#6b6760", hjust = 0,
                                 margin = margin(b = 14)),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = 9,  colour = "#aaa", hjust = 1),
    axis.title    = element_text(size = 11, face = "italic"),
    axis.text     = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5)
  )

element_text() arguments

Argument Values Description
face "plain", "bold", "italic", "bold.italic" Font weight/style
size Number (pts) Font size
colour Colour name or hex Text colour
family Font family name e.g. "sans", "serif", "mono"
hjust 0–1 Horizontal alignment
vjust 0–1 Vertical alignment
angle Degrees Rotation
lineheight Number Line spacing
margin margin(t,r,b,l) Space around text

Full Styling Example from Source

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title    = "Title of the plot",
       subtitle = "Subtitle of the plot",
       caption  = "This is the caption",
       tag      = "Fig. 1") +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(
      family     = "serif",
      face       = "bold",
      colour     = 4,          # colour index 4 = blue
      size       = 15,
      hjust      = 1,
      vjust      = 1,
      angle      = -10,
      lineheight = 1,
      margin     = margin(20, 0, 0, 0)   # t, r, b, l
    ),
    plot.subtitle          = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.caption           = element_text(hjust = 0.25),
    plot.tag               = element_text(face = "italic"),
    plot.title.position    = "plot",    # align title to full width
    plot.caption.position  = "panel",
    plot.tag.position      = "top"
  )
TipRemember: TRBL for margins

The margin() function takes Top, Right, Bottom, Left — remember the word TRouBLe.

margin(t = 20, r = 10, b = 5, l = 10)   # named args
margin(20, 10, 5, 10)                    # positional
